content:
Last Friday (21st), during the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China case, in the early hours, a woman passerby who was queuing to observe the hearing was taken onto a police vehicle by officers. The police, when responding to enquiries, stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "with seditious intent".

In the early hours of last Friday at around 5am, more than fifty people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts to enter the court for observation. During the queue, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of her clothing possibly carrying some seditious intent", and took her onto a police vehicle. While the officers were taking the woman away, several police officers kept directing reporters at the scene to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and at the same time extended the orange cordon line towards the direction of Sai Cheung Street. Only after the woman boarded the police vehicle did they withdraw the cordon. A "court observer" who was queuing near the woman that day pointed out that she was wearing a black T-shirt printed with Japanese text.

{"Collective Gazette" (集誌社) made enquiries to the police regarding the reasons for the woman's removal and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (24th) stating that during a security operation conducted within the West Kowloon Court area on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "with seditious intent", and is being detained for investigation.
